title: REQ-ARC-WMTE-6013: close the change gate's hidden-state coverage hole
substrate_note: No GPU, no model, no LLM. Pure numpy over cached offline-arcade transitions from e3.collect_transitions, scored through the production select_trusted_world_model. GGUF names appear nowhere because none is invoked.

model_specs.note: no model invoked; pure numpy over cached offline-arcade transitions
model_specs.engines_scored: real on-disk results/arc_e3/<game>/world_model.py via e3.load_engine, plus constructed identity / spurious-writer / hand-written control arms

FINDING_pure_invented_write_separation.note: The purer quantity (cells written where reality changed NOTHING) as distinct from spurious_changed_cells (which also counts wrong-valued predictions at genuinely changed cells). Published as calibration input for a follow-up decision; NOT a gate condition in this change.
FINDING_pure_invented_write_separation.why_not_shipped_as_a_gate: The separation is measured against an engine CONSTRUCTED to invent a cell on every transition. That says nothing about where a realistically imperfect induced engine sits, and a threshold fitted to this gap would reject one. Recalibration against an imperfect engine is the prerequisite.

FINDING_gate_must_not_ship_without_mask: Measured through the production path on the WHOLE dc22 corpus, the hand-written correct engine scores change_fidelity 0.4694/0.4083/0.4103 with the mask OFF (REJECTED 3/3, reason change_fidelity_below_threshold) and 0.8148/0.7609/0.7358 with it ON (admitted 3/3). The gate-only arm therefore rejects the one engine known to be genuinely good. Do not flip CARNOT_ARC_WM_CHANGE_GATE without also flipping CARNOT_ARC_WM_HUD_MASK.
FINDING_original_run_mask_arm_was_a_sile: The ORIGINAL exp6013 run passed a real mask but never set CARNOT_ARC_WM_HUD_MASK, so every mask=1 row recorded hud_mask_status='disabled' and change_fidelity differed between mask=0 and mask=1 on 0 of 162 paired arms. acceptance_gate_mask_arm_actually_masked now makes that state unreportable.

interpretation.what_this_does_not_show: This is an OFFLINE decision-level measurement. It shows the repaired gate admits and rejects the engines it should on real cached transitions. It does NOT show a live win-rate effect -- no episode was played, no plan executed, no level solved. The live four-arm A/B is the separate measurement that can speak to that, and nothing here should be read as a substitute for it.
interpretation.mask_and_gate_are_not_independent_on_the: The hand-written control's admission is mask-sensitive. On the WHOLE dc22 corpus the mask-off gate REJECTS it on every seed (3/3) and the mask-on gate ADMITS it on every seed (3/3). Shipping the gate WITHOUT the mask therefore rejects the one engine known to be genuinely good. The earlier wording of this field ('Where mask-off rejects it...') hedged a fact that is not conditional, and the artifact it was written against had a mask arm that never masked; both are corrected here.
interpretation.held_out_split_vs_whole_corpus: This experiment decides on the HELD-OUT split that select_trusted_world_model owns (n_changing 32/28/28 on dc22), while the direct whole-corpus measurement quoted above uses all 120 transitions (n_changing 89/80/91 mask-off). The two populations differ by ~3x and the control sits within 0.035 of the 0.5 threshold on the split, so its verdict there is not robust. Whole-corpus is the figure to quote for a flip decision; the split figure is what the LIVE code path actually computes. Both are reported rather than reconciled away.
interpretation.flag_state: Nothing was flipped. SUBMITTED_WORLD_MODEL_HUD_MASK_ENABLED=False, SUBMITTED_WORLD_MODEL_CHANGE_GATE_ENABLED=False, SUBMITTED_WORLD_MODEL_CHANGE_GATE_HIDDEN_STATE_ENABLED=None (follow). The arms above are selected by passing hud_mask explicitly and by reading the gate's computed record, never by mutating a shipped constant.

verifier_is_oracle_note: TRUE and deliberately so. The engines here are graded against the recorded true next grids, which ARE the oracle for dynamics prediction. This is a measurement of a GATE's discrimination, not a moat claim, and none of these numbers is headline- or gate-flip-eligible on their own.

freshness_acknowledgements.reason: `_state_key` was changed so that negative / non-integer 2-D grids key into the SAME namespace as the arithmetic fast path instead of falling out to `to_ascii` (a `bytes` vs `str` split that broke the PARTITION contract). For every 2-D non-negative integer grid -- which is every grid any ARC engine produces -- the emitted key is unchanged.
freshness_acknowledgements.evidence: 5,200 random 2-D non-negative integer grids (1x1..64x64, colours 0..255, six integer dtypes) keyed under the pre-change and post-change implementations: 0 differed, i.e. bit-identical on the whole class. All 10 games in outer_loop_arc_state_key_dedup_xgame_20260730 report logical_dtype int16 with no negative root colour, so no real grid leaves that class. Re-run end to end on lp85, sk48 and sc25 at a 20,000-engine-call cap: PARTITION_IDENTICAL by accept-trace SHA256, identical unique-state counts and identical plans. The docstring edit is prose.

freshness_acknowledgements.reason: The induce path gains two things and neither is reachable from any code these artifacts execute. (1) `LocalGGUFProposer.generate()` adds `repeat_penalty`/`repeat_last_n` to the llama-server `/completion` payload, guarded by `if codeonly_eligible` -- so it is present ONLY on a live induce call and absent on every other call shape, refactor included. (2) A candidate that parses and defines the required functions is now dry-run/AST-checked via `arc_engine_static_validation.validate_engine_code`, and on a mechanical defect is re-asked once with a neutral block. Both are LIVE-GENERATION behaviours: they change what a running llama-server is asked for and whether its answer is accepted. Also added: a `n_induce_defect_reasks` counter and its `llm.induce_defect_reasks` witness key (a new key, never a changed one), and a new keyword-only `engine_transitions=None` argument whose default reproduces the old call exactly. The defect gate cannot turn a previously-successful call into a failure: it only ever spends one further attempt, and only while an attempt remains (`attempt < tries - 1`), which is pinned by `tests/python/test_arc_induce_repeat_penalty_and_reask_2026_07_31.py`.
freshness_acknowledgements.evidence: DIFFERENTIAL EXECUTION AT THE ARTIFACT LEVEL, not a reading of the diff: this artifact was REBUILT under the changed module using its own recorded `rebuild_command` (canonical repo path, `CARNOT_ARC_E3_DIR` preserved), and the rebuild was deep-diffed leaf-by-leaf against the published version -- 7,390 leaves compared, 0 substantive fields moved. Zero non-annotation fields moved at all -- every population count, decision arm and disagreement row is bit-identical. The rebuild output is retained OUT of tree at `scratchpad/phase2/after/experiment_6013_hidden_state_change_gate_closure.json`. The rebuild was then DISCARDED and the published artifact restored, because regenerating it drops annotations the generator does not emit: it wiped this artifact's `original_timings_superseded_by_rebuild` block and all 4 prior `freshness_acknowledgements`. That is the exact trap the block itself warns about -- 'When the only drift is timing, acknowledge rather than rebuild' -- recorded when commit 0da7f75ad overwrote these same measured timings. So the rebuild was used as PROOF of inertness and not as the artifact of record, which is strictly stronger evidence than an acknowledgement argued from the source diff.
freshness_acknowledgements.why_not_rebuilt: Rebuilding regenerates the artifact from scratch and the generator does not re-emit post-hoc provenance, so a rebuild DROPS this artifact's accumulated `freshness_acknowledgements` and (where present) its `original_timings_superseded_by_rebuild` block -- verified, not assumed: the rebuilds were actually performed and the drop measured. Measured wall-clock is not reproducible, so overwriting it destroys the record of what the original run cost. This follows the guidance the artifacts themselves carry from commit 0da7f75ad: 'When the only drift is timing, acknowledge rather than rebuild.'

freshness_acknowledgements.reason: The 2026-07-31 adversarial-review pass makes exactly ONE behavioural change to this file, and it NARROWS the induce sampler rather than widening it. `repeat_penalty`/`repeat_last_n` were gated on `codeonly_eligible` alone, which is also True for `_split_induce`'s focused goal-only call (`required=('is_level_complete',)`) -- a prompt shape Phase 1 never measured. They are now gated on `_engine_induce_call` (`codeonly_eligible AND 'engine' in required`), the same condition the defect gate already used. Everything else in the diff is comment, plus a named `_engine_induce_call` binding whose value is identical to the `_defect_check_on` it feeds. The affected fields appear ONLY on a live llama-server /completion payload, so the change cannot reach any artifact that makes no live induce call, and where it could reach one it REMOVES a field from a call shape these artifacts do not make.
freshness_acknowledgements.evidence: Proven by DIFFERENTIAL EXECUTION at the artifact level, not argued from reading the diff. This artifact was rebuilt from its own recorded rebuild_command AGAINST THE CHANGED SOURCE and deep-diffed leaf by leaf against the published copy. 7,397 leaves compared; 43 fields differ and ALL 43 are timing or provenance -- SUBSTANTIVE MOVEMENT ZERO, bit-identical on every population count and decision arm. The rebuild's own `provenance.code` entry for this dependency was verified to record sha 85f371ff2a8be824... (the post-change file), because an earlier attempt was invalidated when a concurrent process reverted the working tree mid-run and the rebuild silently used the pre-change source; that check is why this evidence is trustworthy. The rebuild was then DISCARDED and the published artifact restored byte-identically (verified with cmp), because rebuilding also drops this artifact's accumulated `freshness_acknowledgements` and its `original_timings_superseded_by_rebuild` block -- which is itself the record of the previous time this happened, and which instructs 'When the only drift is timing, acknowledge rather than rebuild.' Written up in docs/research-notes/arc-induce-repeat-penalty-wired-2026-07-31.md under 'W4 - SCOPE NARROWED' and in ops/changelog.md.

freshness_acknowledgements.evidence: PROVEN BY REBUILD, not argued. Ran this artifact's own recorded rebuild_command against the changed source and compared the result to the published file LEAF BY LEAF (7403 leaves). Substantive movement: ZERO. The only differing keys were the 8 fields of the `original_timings_superseded_by_rebuild` block, which the rebuild DROPS -- the same destructive behaviour recorded at commit 0da7f75ad, and the reason that block's own `the_preferred_path_next_time` field names acknowledgement rather than rebuild as the correct move here. The rebuild was therefore treated as EVIDENCE and discarded; the published artifact was restored and verified byte-identical to HEAD. The rebuild changed nothing substantive -- verified here by asserting that every differing field is a timing or a provenance hash -- but a wall-clock number is not reproducible, so overwriting it destroys the record of what the first run actually cost.
